ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the input X(t) is divided into upper and lower parallel branches. The upper branch passes through an LTI system labeled H(f)=j2πf, and then enters the positive terminal of the summer; the lower branch is a direct path and enters the negative terminal of the summer. The output of the summer is Y(t). Then reason: From the positive and negative sign relationship in the figure, the equivalent system frequency response is G(f)=H(f)-1=j2πf-1. It is known that the autocorrelation function R_x(τ)=exp(-πτ^2). According to the Fourier transform pair exp(-πτ^2) ↔ exp(-πf^2), the input power spectral density is S_x(f)=exp(-πf^2). The output power spectral density satisfies S_y(f)=|G(f)|^2 S_x(f). Among them, |j2πf-1|^2=(-1)^2+(2πf)^2=1+4π^2f^2. Therefore S_y(f)=(4π^2 f^2+1)exp(-πf^2).

method.method_draft: From the image, combine the parallel branches into one equivalent LTI system with transfer G(f)=H(f)-1=j2πf-1 because the filtered upper branch is added and the direct lower branch is subtracted. From the text, Rx(τ)=exp(-πτ^2), so Sx(f)=F{Rx}=exp(-πf^2). Then compute |G(f)|^2=|j2πf-1|^2=4π^2f^2+1. Therefore Sy(f)=|G(f)|^2Sx(f)=(4π^2f^2+1)exp(-πf^2).
